subject: Post-demo recap: concurrency & streaming SLOs + dedicated validation plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@quantify.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@quantify.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: concurrency & streaming SLOs + dedicated validation plan

Thanks again for the demo time today — good discussion. I wanted to capture the agreed-upon targets and propose a focused validation plan so we keep momentum. Please confirm anything I got wrong.

Key SLOs you called out (as discussed):
- Streaming 1:1 assistant (token streaming): 99th pct latency <= 150ms from first token for sessions with avg output length ~120 tokens
- Peak request throughput: sustained 500 requests/sec (95th pct over 2min windows) during business hours
- Concurrency: ~80 concurrent active sessions (KV cache expected to be warm for ~60% of requests)
- Cold-start latency budget: 99th pct <= 350ms for cold sessions (cache miss)

Model and workload details you provided:
- Primary model: QAI-70B (FP16 / quantized variants will be evaluated)
- Average generated tokens per request: 120
- Fraction of streaming sessions needing function/tool calls: ~12%

Recommended immediate next steps (validation-focused):
1) Redwood provides a 3x GPU matrix test plan (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L4-48GB) and baseline scripts.
2) Quantify AI supplies a 10k sample of anonymized traces (or an S3 link) we can replay plus 2 representative prompt categories.
3) Run staged validation: synthetic ramp (to 500 rps), warmed KV runs, and mixed cold/warm runs to measure 99/95/50 pct latencies and token throughput.
4) Pilot: 2-week reserved throughput pilot on the selected GPU family with auto-scaling knobs disabled to measure steady-state cost and tail latency.

Attachments: validation-plan.xlsx (detailed test matrix), gpu-benchmark-matrix.pdf (expected perf characteristics).

Can you confirm availability of sample traces and whether the model variant will be the 70B non-quantized checkpoint for initial run? If yes, we can schedule the first validation window as early as next week.

Thanks,
Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0147
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@quantify.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: concurrency & streaming SLOs + dedicated validation plan

Diego — thanks, this summary looks right. A couple of clarifying points before we hand over traces: 

1) Concurrency definition: when you say 80 concurrent sessions, do you mean 80 active streaming connections (i.e., token-by-token stream) or 80 in-flight requests overall (including short sync calls)? We primarily care about streaming tail latency.
2) Model variant: for the initial run we plan to use the standard QAI-70B FP16 checkpoint (no quantization) — we will want a follow-up run on a 4-bit quantized variant if the baseline looks promising.
3) What are the expected reserved throughput units? Is 500 rps mapped to a specific slot/unit in your Dedicated offering, or do you recommend we size by GPU count + reserved slots?

If you can outline the mapping (e.g., 1 reserved slot on H100 supports ~X tokens/sec for QAI-70B) that would help our internal sizing/procurement team. We can provide the S3 link to sanitized traces by Monday.

—Tom
Director of ML Ops | Quantify AI
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@quantify.ai>, Elena Park <elena.park@quantify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: concurrency & streaming SLOs + dedicated validation plan

Tom — great questions. Short answers up front, full plan attached.

1) Concurrency: we will size for 80 concurrent streaming connections (token stream open) as the primary gating metric. In our test plan we'll also measure in-flight short sync calls but streaming tail is the SLO.

2) Reserved throughput mapping (high-level):
- H100-80GB (typical perf for QAI-70B FP16): one H100 slot at reserved capacity is expected to sustain ~120-160 steady rps for streaming sessions (avg 120 tokens) with tail latencies near SLO when KV cache is warm.
- A100-80GB: slightly lower steady rps (~90-130 rps) for same tail; better cost per token for some workloads.
- L4-48GB: lower throughput (~30-50 rps) but significantly cheaper per-hour — good fit for non-critical dev/pilot traffic or parallelizing many small sessions.

These numbers are estimates; validation run will produce precise tokens/sec curves. Based on target 500 rps sustained, starting guidance is: 3x H100 slots (reserve 3) or 4x A100 slots (reserve 4) as a baseline. L4 would require many more instances and is not recommended for primary production SLOs.

3) Validation plan highlights (see attached validation-plan.xlsx):
- Runs: cold-start baseline, warmed cache baseline, synthetic ramp to 600 rps, sustained 500 rps for 30-minute windows, and long-run 12-hour soak.
- Metrics: 99/95/50 pct latency for first-token and last-token, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, mem/KV cache hit rate, and error rates for function calls.
- Test data: we will run with your S3 traces plus a small synthetic corpus to push edge cases.

Proposed pilot schedule:
- Mon 16 Aug: exchange S3 access and finalize the validation matrix.
- Tue 17 Aug: run baseline & cold-start tests.
- Wed 18 Aug: ramp tests + short soak.
- If results are within expected margin, we can provision a 2-week reserved throughput pilot starting Mon 23 Aug.

Attachments included: validation-plan.xlsx, gpu-benchmark-matrix.pdf. I'll have Ben (SE) own the perf runs; Marissa will shadow procurement/pricing.

Diego
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
